references.text: The word תֵּבַת (teba, 'ark' or 'chest') is used only twice in the Bible: here about the basket Moses was placed in, and about Noah's ark. Both were sealed with pitch/tar to protect against water.
Both Noah's ark and Moses' basket were sealed with pitch (חֵמָר/זֶפֶת) to make them watertight, and both served as means of rescue through the water.
The continuation of the story where the basket is found at the bank of the Nile by Pharaoh's daughter.
Isaiah mentions boats made of reeds/papyrus (גֹּמֶא) that were used on the water, the same material Moses' basket was made from.
Reference to reeds (סוּף) by Egypt's rivers, the same word used for the place where the basket was placed.
Job mentions papyrus/reeds (גֹּמֶא) that grow by water, the same material used to make Moses' basket.
The Letter to the Hebrews describes how Moses' parents hid him in faith for three months because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they were not afraid of the king's command.
Stephen's speech in Acts refers to this event and tells how Moses was set out and taken up by Pharaoh's daughter.
A parallel between two mothers who had to entrust their chosen sons to God's protection in nature to save them from death.
A strong thematic parallel between two mothers who had to flee with their chosen sons into the desert/water to save them from death.
